Configured names cannot introduce path separators or shell syntax, and the suggested cleanup command is printed rather than executed. No introduced security vulnerability was established. Residual risk concerns trusting configuration to identify disposable content and the inability to restore deleted ignored files. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details
**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The affected assets are ignored files inside eligible local linked worktrees. Configured additions affect reclaim only; the new built-in names also affect prune-wt --yes. Existing root, repository, registration, branch, and state checks constrain deletion targets rather than granting arbitrary filesystem deletion. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — Configuration becomes an authority for declaring additional ignored components disposable. This is an intentional per-machine override within an existing configuration trust domain: the same local file already supplies repository and worktree roots. Whether untrusted processes can write that file is not established. - _observed_ — Configured names cannot contain path separators or shell metacharacters. The refusal command quotes the worktree and each literal Git pathspec and is only printed. Added tests cover quote-containing and glob-like filenames, but those tests were inspected rather than executed during this assessment. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _inferred_ — Eligibility and process checks are snapshots rather than a transaction with deletion. Newly permitted components inherit this existing concurrency limitation. Non-forced removal and post-removal verification help detect refusal or incomplete removal, but do not provide rollback for ignored content. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — Document explicitly that approving a component authorizes deletion of all ignored descendants, including nested secrets or manually saved files. Treat additions as disposal policy and restrict configuration writes to principals trusted to make that decision.
